chapterName: Early Republic: The Conflict of the Orders - Toward Resolution (450-367 BCE)

questions.question: In which year was a plebeian first elected praetor?
questions.explanation: Plebeians had to wait thirty years after the compromise, until 337 BC, to win the praetorship. Patricians also kept some of the oldest priesthoods for themselves.
questions.sourceQuote: Plebeians had to wait thirty years, until 337 BC, before one of them was elected praetor.

questions.question: According to Livy, what did Camillus vow to the god Apollo during the siege of Veii?
options: The walls of the conquered city
A golden statue on the Capitoline
questions.explanation: Livy says Camillus vowed a tenth of the spoils to Apollo. He also invited Juno, Veii's protecting goddess, to move to Rome.
questions.sourceQuote: According to Livy, Camillus vowed a tenth of the spoils to the god Apollo.

questions.question: Up to which year did consular tribunes govern Rome in many years?
questions.explanation: Consular tribunes ran Rome in many years up to 376 BC. Around 400 BC plebeians began to form the majority of them in some years.
questions.sourceQuote: Consular tribunes governed Rome in many years up to 376 BC.

questions.question: Which fact suggests that the 367 BC consulship law did not actually guarantee power-sharing?
options: The praetorship was abolished in 343 BC
Consular tribunes returned from 360 to 350 BC
No consuls were elected from 355 to 343 BC
Both consuls were plebeians from 366 to 355 BC
Both consuls were patricians from 355 to 343 BC
The Senate annulled the law in 355 BC
questions.explanation: From 355 to 343 BC, both consuls were patricians, so the law clearly did not guarantee sharing. Cornell suggests it may have been a mere administrative adjustment.
questions.sourceQuote: From 355 to 343 BC, both consuls were patricians.

questions.question: A passing citizen, Lucius Albinus, carried the Vestal Virgins and their sacred objects to safety in which city?
questions.explanation: Albinus gave the Vestals a lift on his wagon to Caere, an allied Etruscan coastal city. Aristotle's 'certain Lucius' who saved Rome might have been this same man.
questions.sourceQuote: A passing citizen, Lucius Albinus, gave them a lift on his wagon to Caere, an allied Etruscan city on the coast.

questions.question: According to Livy, which Roman mistakes contributed to the disaster at the Allia? (select all that apply)
options: They attacked at night across the Tiber
They stretched their line dangerously thin
They split the army between two consuls
They failed to consult the gods
They left the reserves inside Rome
questions.explanation: Livy blames the Romans for pitching no camp, neglecting the gods and overextending their line. Brennus struck the reserves on a hill and panic spread.
questions.sourceQuote: Livy says the Romans pitched no camp and failed to consult the gods.

questions.question: Which ancient writers told stories crediting someone other than Camillus with defeating the Gauls or saving Rome? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Diodorus credited an Etruscan army, Strabo credited Caere, and Aristotle reportedly named 'a certain Lucius'. Livy is the source of the Camillus rescue, and Cornell is a modern historian.
questions.sourceQuote: Other ancient writers told different stories.

questions.question: In which years did Romans bury alive a pair of Gauls and a pair of Greeks?
questions.explanation: These burials happened in 228, 216 and 114 BC, even though human sacrifice was not a Roman custom. They show how long the fear of the Gauls lasted.
questions.sourceQuote: In 228, 216 and 114 BC, Romans buried alive a pair of Gauls and a pair of Greeks, although human sacrifice was not a Roman custom.

questions.question: Besides capping holdings of public land, what else did the Licinian land law restrict, and why?
options: Selling plots there, to stop speculation by Greeks
Grazing more than 100 cattle there, to protect common pasture
Building houses there, to keep it open for armies
Planting vines there, to keep land for grain
Hunting there, to preserve sacred groves
Settling foreigners there, to reserve it for citizens
questions.explanation: The law banned grazing more than 100 cattle on public land to protect the pasture poor farmers relied on. Ordinary citizens' own plots were only about half a hectare (one and a quarter acres).
questions.sourceQuote: It also banned grazing more than 100 cattle there, to protect the common pasture poor farmers relied on.

questions.question: What happened in the Plebeian Council in 368 BC, after Camillus resigned as dictator?
options: It passed the land and debt bills but rejected the consulship bill
It elected consular tribunes for the first time in years
It passed the consulship bill but rejected the land and debt bills
It voted to abolish the tribunate
It passed all three bills, which the Senate vetoed
It rejected all three bills of Licinius and Sextius
questions.explanation: The plebeians approved the land and debt measures but turned down the consulship bill. The tribunes insisted on all or nothing, and the full package passed later.
questions.sourceQuote: The plebeians passed the land and debt bills but rejected the consulship bill.
